notes: Both evaluate cavity-occupied TRiC findings (C52, C53, C55, C80-C84). LLM finds evidence sufficient with ~4-5 fold increase and control experiments. Peer reviewers request additional controls with empty TRiCs processed identically, expressing uncertainty about the difference density interpretation despite acknowledging it 'looks nice'.

Both address cavity-occupied vs cavity-empty TRiC classification (C49-C55). LLM considers statistical classification and controls sufficient. Peer reviewers express significant doubt about distinguishing the two classes, stating 'it is difficult to be sure that the difference between them is significant' and requesting quantitative measures to prove the difference is real.

Both evaluate TRiC binding to fibril tips via apical domains (C5, C45, C46, C71). LLM finds 3-D tomography and SPT analysis provide strong structural evidence. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as 'one of the most interesting findings' but state 'the implications of this finding in the context of mHtt fibril formation remain unclear,' indicating acceptance of observation but uncertainty about biological significance.

Both address TRiC binding patterns and fibril interactions (C41, C43, C44). LLM supports the structural evidence from tomography. Peer reviewers request quantitative statistics on binding frequency and ratios, and express concern that 'many of the interactions between the TRiC and the fibrils were lost during sample preparation,' indicating uncertainty about completeness of observations.

Both evaluate experimental design parameters (C56, C57, C58). LLM finds the 1:5 TRiC:mhtt ratio appropriately justified by prior work. Peer reviewers question whether this ratio 'can be physiological' and request elaboration on typical in vivo levels, expressing uncertainty about physiological relevance despite cited justifications.

Both address resolution assessment (C116). LLM finds SPT methodology appropriately validated with FSC-based resolution assessment. Peer reviewers question 'Was the map resolution really isotropic (as mentioned in the Methods section)?' expressing doubt about reported resolution characteristics given tomographic reconstruction limitations.

Partial overlap on cavity-related claims (C47, C48, C52, C81). LLM supports cavity occupation findings. Peer reviewers seek clarification about unbound TRiC population and their cavity contents, though manuscript provides some quantitative data (890 freestanding vs 326 fibril-bound). Different focus: LLM on occupied cavities, reviewers on unbound population characterization.

Minimal overlap (C35, C36) on aggregate prevention observations. LLM supports time-course 2-D cryoEM demonstration of fibril prevention. Peer reviewers' uncertainty focuses on quantitative binding statistics and sample preparation losses, which extends beyond the specific claims in LLM R1 about aggregate morphology observations.

Minimal overlap (C35, C36) on fibril prevention. LLM supports 2-D cryoEM observations of aggregate suppression. Peer reviewers acknowledge TRiC decorating fibril tips as interesting but find implications unclear. Different scopes: LLM on morphological observations, reviewers on mechanistic implications.

Minimal overlap (C103) on experimental conditions. LLM supports overall experimental design following established protocols. Peer reviewers question choice of mhttQ51 (lowest pathogenic Q frequency), asking if this form is most abundant and typical under physiological conditions. Different focus areas within experimental design evaluation.

Minimal overlap (C54) on resolution. LLM supports cavity-occupied findings with acknowledged modest resolution. Peer reviewers question isotropy of resolution specifically. Very limited claim overlap; different aspects of resolution assessment.

LLM evaluates dual mechanism model (C64, C92, C93, C96, C101) integrating fibril capping and oligomer encapsulation. No corresponding peer review result directly addresses this integrated mechanistic model, though individual components are questioned in other peer results.

LLM expresses uncertainty about connections to cellular phenomena (C61, C62, C72, C73, C98), noting in vitro conditions may not recapitulate cellular environment. No corresponding peer review result directly addresses these specific claims about cellular relevance.

LLM expresses uncertainty about mechanistic hypotheses extending beyond direct observations (C68, C70, C74, C75, C87, C88, C99), including N17 domain involvement and dual-end binding. No corresponding peer review result directly addresses these specific mechanistic speculations.
